minutes.headline: Capital committee voted to add Marshall Park master plan and a DPW pickup to the FY22 capital plan.
minutes.summary: The Capital Planning Committee reviewed the FY22 capital plan after the next two prioritized projects (Marshall Park master plan and a DPW three-quarter ton pickup with plow) became fundable, and members voiced support. They moved to support the addition, heard from the town manager's office on the plan's wording in the Town Meeting booklet, and heard counsel's view on how Town Meeting may amend the article. The next meeting was set for April 6.

what_happened.line: The Capital Planning Committee moved to support adding the Marshall Park master plan and a DPW pickup with plow to the FY22 capital plan; the vote count was not audible.
Both projects became fundable after the budget left available and unexpected capital, including money from an old Marshall Park parking article.
The committee agreed to add a line to the Town Meeting booklet saying it is reviewing financial policies related to capital planning.
Members discussed the special purpose stabilization deposit, which brings the fire engine and rescue truck close to being funded without borrowing.
The next meeting was set for April 6 to wrap up policy discussions.

why_it_matters: Town Meeting voters will be asked to approve the FY22 capital article, and these two additions change what is in it.
The stabilization deposit and the borrowing-versus-cash discussion bear on how the town pays for fire apparatus, which affects future debt and tax bills.
